method: A planar four-bar linkage is classified from its four link lengths by the Grashof condition, the shortest link plus the longest against the two others: when that sum is the smaller the shortest link turns through a full circle and the link that is shortest decides the type - the ground link gives a double crank, one of the grounded links a crank-rocker and the coupler a Grashof double rocker - while a larger sum leaves no link able to turn fully (a triple rocker) and an exact equality is a change point where the linkage folds through a dead position; ties are broken in the order ground, input, coupler, output. For a given input angle the end of the crank is placed at the input length from the first pivot, and the coupler joint at the intersection of a circle of radius equal to the coupler about that end and a circle of radius equal to the output link about the second pivot, which is the closed-loop position solution; the two intersections are the two assembly modes, and when the circles miss each other the linkage cannot be assembled at that angle. The rocker angle is measured at the second pivot from the ground line, the coupler angle at the crank end, and the transmission angle is the acute angle between the coupler and the rocker, which reflection leaves the same in both assembly modes. A transmission angle below 40 degrees is the usual practical limit, because the coupler then pushes the rocker mostly along its own length. When the input link is a crank the rocker turns between the two positions where the crank and the coupler lie in line, and that range and its swing are reported. Lengths above 0 and at most 100000 in any single unit, and input angles from 0 to 360 degrees, are accepted; text, exponent notation, a blank field, a zero or negative length and a value outside those ranges are refused with the exact reason, and decimal commas are accepted. Angles are rounded to 12 significant digits. This is the position geometry of an ideal planar linkage with four pin joints: it does not model joint clearance, link deflection, out-of-plane offsets, friction, inertia or the loads the mechanism carries, and it assumes the ground line is horizontal with the input angle measured counter-clockwise from it. It runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Four-bar linkage (Wikipedia): the Grashof condition S + L <= P + Q decides whether the shortest link can turn fully, its classification names the crank-rocker, double crank and double rocker cases, and the ground, input, coupler and output links are defined.

Middle East Technical University, Machine and Mechanism Theory, chapter 7, Four-bar mechanism: the transmission angle is the acute angle between the coupler and the output link, 90 degrees is optimal, and a deviation beyond 40 or 50 degrees makes the mechanism lock.

Union College ESC104, Graphical linkage synthesis: the extreme (toggle) positions occur when the input crank and the coupler lie in line, and the transmission angle should stay between 40 and 120 degrees.
